ANI Press Releases Wondrlab Launches WondrAgents, India’s First Unified Agentic Operating System for End-to-End Influencer Marketing ANI PR 08 September, 2026 04:31 pm IST Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Vandana Verma, Co-Founder, Wondrlab Network, and Shidush Contractor, Chief Operating Officer, OPA & Opportune Follow Us : Text Size: A- A+ PRNewswire Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], September 8: Wondrlab today unveiled WondrAgents, India’s first unified Agentic Operating System for influencer marketing, powering its influencer marketing platforms OPA and Opportune. Built as a network of seven specialised AI agents, WondrAgents seamlessly executes the complete influencer campaign lifecycle, from campaign brief and creator discovery to outreach, negotiation, contracting, content evaluation and ROI reporting, helping brands reduce campaign go-live time by up to 70% while delivering measurable business outcomes. Show Full Article The launch marks the next evolution of Wondrlab’s ‘Total Influence’ vision, bringing together years of influencer marketing expertise, proprietary creator intelligence, campaign learnings and machine learning into a unified operating system that enables brands to execute influencer campaigns with greater speed, transparency and precision. Unlike conventional AI tools that automate individual tasks, WondrAgents is designed as a unified ‘Agentic Operating System’ where seven specialised AI agents work alongside campaign teams to power every stage of campaign execution. Each agent is trained to optimise against a brand’s campaign objectives, from campaign planning and creator discovery to negotiation, content evaluation and performance reporting, while human teams continue to lead strategy, creativity and relationship management. The launch addresses one of the industry’s biggest challenges, where brands continue to rely on disconnected tools, manual coordination and fragmented reporting. By bringing the entire influencer marketing workflow onto a single unified intelligent operating system across OPA and Opportune, our SaaS platforms, WondrAgents enables greater operational efficiency, complete campaign visibility and continuous optimisation throughout the campaign lifecycle. Speaking about the launch, Vandana Verma, Co-Founder, Wondrlab Network, said, “Since 2020, we’ve built one of India’s largest influencer marketing ecosystems through OPA and Opportune. Every campaign we’ve executed has added to the rich knowledge base of creator intelligence, brand insights and campaign learnings. WondrAgents is built on that proprietary knowledge base. We’ve invested significantly in training these agents with years of experience, and we will continue investing in agentic AI because we believe the future of influencer marketing lies in humans and AI agents working together to deliver faster execution, smarter decisions and better outcomes for brands.” Shidush Contractor, Chief Operating Officer, OPA & Opportune, added, “We’re excited to introduce India’s first unified Agentic Operating System for influencer marketing. WondrAgents is built to tackle the toughest campaign briefs, bringing together great minds, specialised AI agents and years of campaign intelligence to execute faster and smarter. From evaluating creators and generating personalised scripts to optimising campaign performance, the platform takes care of the operational complexity, allowing teams to focus on ideas, creativity and strategic decisions. articles.title: First bullet train testing coach ready, Surat-Bilimora section targeted for 2027 commissioning
articles.content: Railways 1 min read First bullet train testing coach ready, Surat-Bilimora section targeted for 2027 commissioning: Vaishnaw The development marks a key phase for India’s first high-speed rail project, with the broader corridor targeted to begin services in August 2027. ET Infra Desk ETInfra Published On Sep 8, 2026 at 02:57 PM IST Select ETInfra as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Vaishnaw said the first coach built for testing the bullet train system is ready, while civil construction on the Vapi-Surat section is expected to be completed by December. India's first high-speed rail project is moving towards its first operational milestone, with the Surat-Bilimora section of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail (MAHSR) corridor targeted for commissioning in 2027, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said on Monday, as cited by ANI. Vaishnaw said the first coach built for testing the bullet train system is ready, while civil construction on the Vapi-Surat section is expected to be completed by December. Advt The developments mark a key phase in the construction of the 508-km Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor, which passes through Maharashtra, Gujarat and the Union Territory of Dadra & Nagar Haveli. Surat-Bilimora to be first operational section The Surat-Bilimora stretch is expected to become the first operational section of the MAHSR project. The broader corridor is targeted to begin high-speed rail services in August 2027. Construction is progressing across multiple sections, the minister said. The project is designed to substantially reduce travel time between Mumbai and Ahmedabad while providing faster, safer and more reliable passenger connectivity. 12 stations on the 508-km corridor The MAHSR corridor will have 12 stations: Mumbai (BKC), Thane, Virar, Boisar, Vapi, Bilimora, Surat, Bharuch, Vadodara, Anand, Ahmedabad and Sabarmati. The stations are being developed with modern passenger facilities and multimodal connectivity, with designs incorporating elements associated with their respective locations. The foundation stone for the project was laid in September 2017, marking the launch of India's high-speed rail programme. articles.title: India's first bullet train to hit tracks by May-June next year: When will services begin?
articles.content: India’s first bullet train to hit tracks by May-June next year: When will services begin? Edited By: Aiswarya Venugopal Last Updated: 08 September 2026, 02:59 PM IST Representational Image | AI Generated India's first indigenously built bullet train is expected to roll onto the tracks for testing by May or June next year, Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has said, offering one of the clearest timelines yet on when the country's high-speed rail project could move closer to commercial operations. The testing phase is expected to last between two and four months, following which the bullet train will be inaugurated, according to the Railway Minister. Speaking at the 'NaMo for Viksit Bharat' event in Vadodara on Tuesday, Vaishnaw said the first body frame of India's own bullet train had recently been completed and sent for a squeeze test. “By May or June of next year, India’s own bullet train will be on the tracks for testing. After a testing period of 2-4 months, the bullet train will be inaugurated by the Prime Minister himself,” he said. First test coach ready as manufacturing gathers pace The latest announcement comes amid rapid progress in the manufacturing of India's first high-speed train. Vaishnaw had earlier said that the first coach for testing had already been manufactured, while work was progressing simultaneously on the railway infrastructure required for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail corridor. Civil construction on the Vapi-Surat section is expected to be completed by December this year. The Surat-Bilimora stretch, meanwhile, has been targeted for commissioning next year. The Railway Minister said the bullet train project was being developed in line with the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat, with India moving towards building its own high-speed rail technology and infrastructure. Vadodara to Mumbai in around 90 minutes One of the biggest changes the bullet train promises is a sharp reduction in travel time between major cities. According to Vaishnaw, passengers travelling from Vadodara to Mumbai on the bullet train will be able to complete the journey in around one-and-a-half hours. The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail project is India's first bullet train corridor and is among the country's most ambitious railway infrastructure projects. The 508-km corridor will pass through Maharashtra, Gujarat and Dadra & Nagar Haveli, connecting Mumbai, Thane, Virar, Boisar, Vapi, Bilimora, Surat, Bharuch, Vadodara, Anand, Ahmedabad and Sabarmati. When will India's bullet train start? While testing is now expected to begin by May or June next year, the first high-speed rail service on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor is expected to commence in August 2027. The project has been progressing in phases, with construction and train manufacturing taking place simultaneously across key sections. The foundation stone for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail corridor was laid in September 2017, marking India's entry into the high-speed rail era. Indian Railways undergoing wider transformation Beyond the bullet train project, Vaishnaw said Indian Railways was undergoing a wider transformation, ranging from operating and reservation systems to construction methods. articles.title: Astrogate Labs Develops India's First Indigenous OISL Terminal - GKToday
articles.content: Home Astrogate Labs Develops India’s First Indigenous OISL Terminal Astrogate Labs Develops India’s First Indigenous OISL Terminal September 8, 2026 Current Affairs Today - Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 Astrogate Labs, an Indian deep-tech startup, has announced the development of India’s first indigenous Optical Inter-Satellite Link (OISL) terminal. The system is designed for direct satellite-to-satellite laser communication and marks a shift from space-to-ground optical links to in-orbit connectivity. Optical Inter-Satellite Link An Optical Inter-Satellite Link uses laser beams for communication between satellites in space. OISL systems are used in satellite constellations, especially in Low Earth Orbit (LEO), where fast data transfer and reduced dependence on ground stations are required. AstroLink Micro and Flight Readiness Astrogate Labs demonstrated its AstroLink Micro system at the 9th Bengaluru Space Expo (BSX 2026) at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre in Karnataka. The system is a 10 Gbps space-to-ground laser communication terminal, and the company has stated that the new OISL terminal is targeted for full flight readiness by 2027. Technology Readiness and Testing Astrogate Labs’ space-to-ground laser communication terminals have reached Technology Readiness Level 8 (TRL 8). TRL 8 is a stage in the technology development scale that indicates a system has been completed and qualified for spaceflight. Important Facts for Exams Optical communication in space uses light, usually laser beams, instead of radio frequency signals. Low Earth Orbit satellites typically operate at altitudes of about 160 km to 2,000 km above Earth. Technology Readiness Levels are used to measure the maturity of a technology from concept to operational deployment. BSX 2026 refers to the 9th Bengaluru Space Expo held at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre. Industry and International Linkages Astrogate Labs has been identified as the sole Indian company to have supplied an indigenously developed satellite-to-ground laser communication terminal to the Indian Space Research Organisation . The startup also completed cross-compatibility testing with the University of Western Australia’s TeraNet mobile optical ground station. India’s Space Communication Ecosystem Satellite laser communication is used for high-speed data transfer, lower latency, and secure links in space systems. End-to-end control of such technology is relevant for future LEO satellite constellations and for indigenous space communication infrastructure. Raising the bar for these everyday experiences, homegrown brand Zebronics has launched the Zeb-Juke Bar 11000, a flagship 1610W RMS home audio system engineered to transform the living room into a private entertainment arena. Anchoring this experience is an 11.2.4 channel setup that envelops listeners in a genuinely three-dimensional soundstage, mirroring the spatial depth found in a proper theatre. By optimizing each frequency independently, it delivers a richer, more detailed soundstage with remarkable depth, balance, and clarity. Powering this performance are substantial dual 20.32cm subwoofer drivers that handle low-frequency duties independently, adding depth and impact to every scene and track. With built-in support for Dolby Atmos and DTS:X, the soundbar accurately decodes high-fidelity audio formats, allowing every scene to unfold with breathtaking realism and spatial accuracy, recreating the scale and immersion of a premium cinema within the comfort of home. Beyond movies and music, the system seamlessly adapts to interactive entertainment. A bundled UHF wireless microphone makes karaoke sessions, celebrations, and casual performances effortless, while True Wireless Home Audio support allows additional compatible speakers to be connected for an even larger synchronized soundstage across expansive or multi-room environments. On the connectivity side, this premium audio setup supports Bluetooth v5.3, TV eARC, Optical IN, USB, and AUX, providing effortless compatibility with televisions, smartphones, gaming consoles, and other entertainment devices. This broad compatibility ensures smooth source-switching without any drop in convenience or audio performance. articles.title: Fortis Healthcare to Install India's First Upright Proton Therapy System
articles.content: Medi News Facebook Twitter Linkedin Patient undergoing positioning in Leo Cancer Care’s Marie® upright proton therapy system New Technology to Advance Precision Cancer Care in India Fortis Healthcare, part of the IHH Healthcare group, has announced plans to install the MEVION S250-FIT™ Proton Therapy System™ at Fortis Memorial Research Institute (FMRI), Gurugram. The system will feature Leo Cancer Care’s Marie® upright positioning technology and RayStation® treatment planning software from RaySearch Laboratories. Subject to regulatory approvals and site preparations, the installation will make Fortis the first healthcare provider in India to introduce upright proton therapy and the first Leo Cancer Care system in the country. Precision and Patient-Centric Treatment Proton therapy can target tumours precisely while reducing radiation exposure to surrounding healthy tissues. This approach can benefit selected adult and paediatric cancers, particularly tumours located near sensitive organs such as the brain, spinal cord, heart and lungs. As per the press release issued by Fortis Healthcare, the system combines a compact proton accelerator with a fixed-beam delivery system, upright positioning and integrated CT imaging. This configuration can also improve comfort for patients who find it difficult to lie flat. Also Read | Three Indian Firms Get SEC Nod for Semaglutide Formulations Strengthening Advanced Cancer Care The compact system can fit within FMRI’s existing infrastructure, reducing the space and construction requirements typically associated with proton therapy. Moreover, its installation will further strengthen the Fortis Cancer Institute’s comprehensive oncology and precision-care capabilities. Dr Ashutosh Raghuvanshi, Managing Director & CEO, Fortis Healthcare, said the initiative will help strengthen India’s precision-oncology capabilities and expand access to advanced cancer treatment. The installation remains subject to applicable regulatory approvals and necessary site preparations.

articles.title: ISRO's Another Milestone - Daily Excelsior
articles.content: The successful placement of EOS-05 into geosynchronous transfer orbit is far more than another entry in ISRO's long list of achievements. It is a milestone that quietly redraws the boundaries of what Indian space technology can do for ordinary citizens, farmers, disaster planners and diplomats alike. At a little over 2,300 kilograms, EOS-05 is the heaviest satellite ever carried by a GSLV rocket, and its significance lies not merely in its weight but in what it represents: India's first arrival as an operator of a dedicated imaging satellite in geo-orbit. This is not an ordinary satellite. Unlike Earth observation platforms that have long circled the planet from low Earth orbit, EOS-05 will hover roughly 36,000 kilometres above Earth, matching the planet's rotational speed. That positioning is what makes it futuristic in a way earlier missions were not: it can provide near real-time, continuous imagery of the same region rather than periodic snapshots. In an era where such persistent, high-resolution monitoring is in ever-growing demand, this capability places India firmly among a select group of nations equipped to watch their own land and neighbourhood with genuine immediacy. It would be a mistake to think of such satellites purely in terms of communication or surveillance. Their real value lies in the quieter, less glamorous work of saving lives and livelihoods. Agricultural output across South Asia remains hostage to the rains and to the health of rivers and glacial lakes. Imagery of the kind EOS-05 will generate can track soil moisture, cropping patterns and water stress well before they translate into shortages, giving planners the lead time to act rather than merely react. The same imaging capability carries an even more urgent application in monitoring glacial lake outburst floods and similar threats. The tragedy that unfolded in Nepal, when a glacial lake burst its banks with devastating consequences, is a stark reminder that a single reliable warning, issued early enough, can spare thousands of lives. A satellite capable of tracking such risks continuously, from a fixed vantage point in the sky, is not a luxury; it is fast becoming a necessity for a region defined by fragile mountains and unpredictable monsoons. There is also a diplomatic dimension worth noting. India has consistently offered to share disaster-related satellite data with neighbouring countries, and EOS-05's imagery could become a genuine instrument of goodwill, extending early warning capabilities to nations that lack such infrastructure of their own. ISRO has made it clear that EOS-05 is not a "spy satellite", and its stated purpose is civilian, which is not in doubt. But it would be naive to ignore the strategic subtext of this launch. A nation that has now demonstrated the ability to place a satellite of this mass and sophistication into geosynchronous orbit has, by extension, proven the underlying rocketry and payload capacity that any future dedicated defence or reconnaissance satellite would require.
